- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.75.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and recent price is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if volatility >1.5% over last 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if 18-day average is >10% above recent 5-day high, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5 periods.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model tends to overreact; apply 1–2% downward correction to forecast if sentiment remains flat for 3+ consecutive days.
